"Millionaire Bucks" has had no $5 million top prize claimed for close to two months. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

The table below shows the full count for "Millionaire Bucks", with every prize level included.
952.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

959.body:
The top prize count on "LOTERIA®" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has two of eight top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

If you play "LOTERIA®" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
959.headline: Good news: no big claims

972.body:
The top prize count on "$8 Million Money Maker" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has one of five top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

For "$8 Million Money Maker" or any game, being late in a run is not automatically good or bad. The same numbers mean different things near the end of a run.

If "$8 Million Money Maker" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
972.headline: Top prizes are still left

975.body:
"$1,000,000 Money Rush" offers a top prize of $1 million and eleven prize levels in all. The prize money leans toward small, frequent prizes. Games shaped like this pay out often, in small amounts. This design never changes, while every other number on this page does.

The numbers for "$1,000,000 Money Rush" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
975.headline: The prize mix in this game

976.body:
The top prize on "100X The Cash" is $2 million, but the most anyone can win today is $10,000. The biggest prize left is far smaller than the one shown on the ticket. Both amounts come from the official prize table. Every top prize has been claimed, and the table shows what is left at each level.

The numbers for "100X The Cash" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
976.headline: Top prize gone for a while

980.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "20X The Cash", about a quarter are still unsold. The game is in the second half of its run, with three of eight top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Today's free summary of "20X The Cash" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
980.headline: How much has sold

981.body:
"50X The Cash" has one of six top prizes left and is close to selling out. Most of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

Everything above about "50X The Cash" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
981.headline: Early stage or late

985.body:
"MAX-A-MILLION" has twelve of 25 top prizes left and is near the midpoint of its run. About half of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

Every line of MAX-A-MILLION's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
985.headline: Early stage or late

988.body:
The most common win left on "Emerald 10's" is $10. The second biggest prize left is $50,000, and three of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Everything above about "Emerald 10's" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
988.headline: Prize table details

990.body:
"LADY LUCK" has two of four top prizes left and is well into its run. About three-quarters of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, tickets are selling faster than top prizes are being claimed, which is good for the tickets that are left.

Everything here about "LADY LUCK" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through November 12.
990.headline: How much has sold

992.body:
"$2 MILLION VAULT" is well into its run, with about a quarter of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, tickets are selling faster than top prizes are being claimed, which is good for the tickets that are left.

If "$2 MILLION VAULT" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
992.headline: Early stage or late

993.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "$5,000 Triple Play" are sold. The top prize count has held, with three of six still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

The numbers for "$5,000 Triple Play" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
993.headline: No top prize claimed lately

994.body:
"$25,000 Triple Play" has 111,536 prizes of $2 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $3,000 prize, with three left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

The numbers for "$25,000 Triple Play" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
